records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron in [the] land of Egypt, saying,
pieces: In the land of Egypt, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and to Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

R.1: While Moses and Aaron were still in Egypt, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to them,

decisions.choice: in the land of Egypt: the one body of law given before Sinai
decisions.reason: Almost all of Israel's laws are given at Mount Sinai or on the way to the promised land. The Passover laws are set apart as given in Egypt itself, on the eve of the departure, so that the feast is tied to the event it remembers.

decisions.choice: to Moses and to Aaron: God speaks to both, who pass the word to the people
decisions.reason: The instructions are addressed to both brothers (as in 6:13 and 7:8), and Moses passes them on to the elders in verse 21.

decisions.choice: While ... were still in Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why the place is named: the law came before they left Egypt.

records.heading: The Passover

records.source: הַחֹ֧דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם רֹ֣אשׁ חֳדָשִׁ֑ים רִאשׁ֥וֹן הוּא֙ לָכֶ֔ם לְחָדְשֵׁ֖י הַשָּׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: This month [will be] for you [the] head of months; first it [will be] for you of [the] months of the year.
pieces: "From now on this month is to head your calendar: count it as the first month of your year.

L.2: "This month [shall be] for you the head of months; it [shall be] the first of the months of the year for you.

R.2: "This month will now begin your calendar. It will be the first month of the year for you.

decisions.choice: the head of months: the month that begins the year
decisions.reason: "Head" means the first in order, as the second half of the verse explains. Israel's year of festivals is to be counted from the month of the exodus.

decisions.choice: this month: the spring month Abib, later called Nisan
decisions.reason: The month is named Abib, "fresh ears of grain", in 13:4, 23:15 and 34:18, and later Nisan (Nehemiah 2:1; Esther 3:7). It falls in March to April. Exodus also speaks of the harvest feast "at the going out of the year" (23:16), a reckoning of the year from the autumn, so this verse fixes the order of the sacred year without ruling out the other.

decisions.choice: for you: plural, all Israel
decisions.reason: "You" is plural here and through the instructions that follow. God speaks to Moses and Aaron, but the commands are for the whole people and their households.

decisions.choice: From now on / now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "now" to show that this is a new reckoning of the year, which the Hebrew implies by setting it at this moment.

records.source: דַּבְּר֗וּ אֶֽל־כָּל־עֲדַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֶּעָשֹׂ֖ר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְיִקְח֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם אִ֛ישׁ שֶׂ֥ה לְבֵית־אָבֹ֖ת שֶׂ֥ה לַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: Speak to all [the] congregation of Israel, saying, on [the] tenth of this month, and they will take for themselves each man a lamb for [a] house of fathers, a lamb for the house.
pieces: Speak to the whole community of Israel and tell them: 'On the tenth day of this month the head of every family is to pick out a lamb, one lamb to a household.

L.3: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, 'On the tenth of this month they shall take for themselves, each man, a lamb for a father's house, a lamb for the household.

R.3: Tell the whole community of Israel this: 'On the tenth day of this month, the man who leads each family must choose a lamb. Each household needs one lamb.

decisions.choice: congregation: Israel as one gathered community
decisions.reason: This is the first time the word is used for Israel. It means a body of people who meet and act together, and it becomes a regular name for Israel in the wilderness (16:1-2; Numbers 1:2). The whole people, household by household, is to keep the Passover.

decisions.choice: lamb: one young animal from the flock, a sheep or a goat
decisions.reason: The word means a single animal of the flock and covers both sheep and goats, as verse 5 says.

decisions.choice: each man ... a father's house: the head of each household
decisions.reason: A "father's house" is a family under its male head, often with grown sons and their families. The man is the head of his household, who acts for all who live in it.

decisions.choice: community
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "community", the everyday word, as in 12:47; Literal keeps "congregation".

decisions.choice: the head of every family / the man who leads each family
decisions.reason: "Each man" here is the man at the head of each household (m3), so Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְאִם־יִמְעַ֣ט הַבַּיִת֮ מִהְיֹ֣ת מִשֶּׂה֒ וְלָקַ֣ח ה֗וּא וּשְׁכֵנ֛וֹ הַקָּרֹ֥ב אֶל־בֵּית֖וֹ בְּמִכְסַ֣ת נְפָשֹׁ֑ת אִ֚ישׁ לְפִ֣י אָכְל֔וֹ תָּכֹ֖סּוּ עַל־הַשֶּֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And if is too small the household for being for a lamb, then will take he and his neighbor the near to his house, by [the] number of persons; each man according to [the] mouth of his eating you will count for the lamb.
pieces: Should a household be too small for a whole lamb, the man is to join with the neighbor who lives closest and take one between them, counting the people in both homes. Divide the lamb by how much each one will eat.

L.4: And if the household is too small for a lamb, then he and his neighbor near to his house shall take [one], according to the number of persons; according to what each one eats you shall make your count for the lamb.

R.4: Some households may be too small to eat a whole lamb. Then they should share one with their closest neighbors. Count the people and think about how much each one can eat, so you will know how many can share a lamb.

decisions.choice: each one according to his eating: by how much each person eats
decisions.reason: The phrase reads "each according to the mouth of his eating". The people sharing a lamb are to be counted so that it is eaten up and nothing is left over (verse 10).

decisions.choice: his neighbor near to his house: the household next door
decisions.reason: A small household joins with the closest one, so that two families share one animal and one meal.

decisions.choice: so you will know how many can share a lamb
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the purpose of the counting, which the Hebrew implies.

records.source: שֶׂ֥ה תָמִ֛ים זָכָ֥ר בֶּן־שָׁנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם מִן־הַכְּבָשִׂ֥ים וּמִן־הָעִזִּ֖ים תִּקָּֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: A lamb unblemished, male, son of a year it will be for you; from the sheep and from the goats you will take [it].
pieces: It must be a sound, unblemished male in its first year, picked from either the sheep or the goats.

L.5: [Your] lamb shall be without blemish, a male, a son of a year; from the sheep or from the goats you shall take [it].

R.5: The animal must be a healthy one-year-old male with nothing wrong with it. It can be a young sheep or a young goat.

decisions.choice: lamb: a young sheep or a young goat
decisions.reason: The animal of verse 3 may be taken from the sheep or from the goats; a young goat is just as fitting as a young sheep.

decisions.choice: unblemished: whole, with no defect
decisions.reason: The word means complete and sound. Animals offered to God had to be free of injury and disease (Leviticus 22:19-22).

decisions.choice: son of a year: a year old, in its first year
decisions.reason: "Son of a year" is the Hebrew way of giving an age. It describes an animal in its first year (Leviticus 23:12).

decisions.choice: sound, unblemished
decisions.reason: Balanced uses two words to show that the animal must be both healthy and free of any mark or injury.

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה לָכֶם֙ לְמִשְׁמֶ֔רֶת עַ֣ד אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְשָׁחֲט֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ כֹּ֛ל קְהַ֥ל עֲדַֽת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it will be for you for keeping until [the] fourteenth day of this month, and will slaughter it all [the] assembly of [the] congregation of Israel between the two evenings.
pieces: Look after it until the fourteenth day of this month. On that day, as evening falls, the whole assembled community of Israel is to slaughter their lambs.

L.6: And it shall be kept by you until the fourteenth day of this month, and all the assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it between the two evenings.

R.6: Take care of the animal until the fourteenth day of the month. Then, as the sun goes down that evening, all the people of Israel must kill their animals.

decisions.choice: between the two evenings: at twilight, as the day ends
alternatives: in the late afternoon, before sunset
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for the Passover (Leviticus 23:5; Numbers 9:3) and for the daily evening offering (29:39-41). Its exact meaning is uncertain. It may mean between sunset and dark, or between the sun's turning toward evening in the afternoon and sunset. Deuteronomy 16:6 says the Passover is slaughtered "in the evening, at the going down of the sun".

decisions.choice: all the assembly of the congregation: the whole people, at one time
decisions.reason: Each household slaughters its own animal (verse 3), but all of Israel does it together, at the same hour. "It" is the lamb of each household.

decisions.choice: for keeping: kept safe and watched over
decisions.reason: The animal is chosen on the tenth day and kept with care for four days, so that it stays unblemished until the fourteenth.

decisions.choice: their lambs / their animals
decisions.reason: "It" means each household's animal, so Balanced and Readable use the plural.

records.source: וְלָֽקְחוּ֙ מִן־הַדָּ֔ם וְנָֽתְנ֛וּ עַל־שְׁתֵּ֥י הַמְּזוּזֹ֖ת וְעַל־הַמַּשְׁק֑וֹף עַ֚ל הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־יֹאכְל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they will take from the blood and put [it] on the two doorposts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they will eat it.
pieces: Some of the blood is to go on the two doorposts and on the lintel of each house where the lamb is eaten.

L.7: And they shall take some of the blood and put [it] on the two doorposts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they eat it.

R.7: Then they must take some of the blood and smear it on the door frame of each house where they will eat the meat: on both side posts and on the beam across the top.

decisions.choice: the two doorposts and the lintel: the frame of the doorway
decisions.reason: The doorposts are the upright posts on either side of the door, and the lintel is the beam across the top. The blood marks the entrance, the boundary between the house and the night outside (verses 22-23).

decisions.choice: door frame ... side posts ... the beam across the top
decisions.reason: Readable explains "doorposts" and "lintel". Literal and Balanced keep the terms.

records.source: וְאָכְל֥וּ אֶת־הַבָּשָׂ֖ר בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַזֶּ֑ה צְלִי־אֵ֣שׁ וּמַצּ֔וֹת עַל־מְרֹרִ֖ים יֹאכְלֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And they will eat the meat in this night, roasted [with] fire, and unleavened bread with bitter herbs they will eat it.
pieces: The meat is to be eaten that night, fire-roasted, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

L.8: And they shall eat the meat in this night, roasted with fire; with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they shall eat it.

R.8: They must roast the meat over a fire and eat it that night. They must eat it with bread made without yeast and with bitter herbs.

decisions.choice: unleavened bread: flat bread made without leaven
decisions.reason: The dough was baked without a lump of fermented dough to make it rise, so it could be made quickly. Verses 34 and 39 tell how the people left in such haste that their dough had no time to rise.

decisions.choice: bitter herbs: bitter plants, kinds not named
decisions.reason: The word means bitter things, here bitter leaves eaten with the meal. The text does not say what they stand for. The same root is used in 1:14, where the Egyptians made the Israelites' lives bitter.

decisions.choice: bread made without yeast
decisions.reason: Readable says "yeast" for leaven. In ancient times bread was raised with a piece of old, fermented dough, not with yeast as it is sold today, but the effect is the same.

records.source: אַל־תֹּאכְל֤וּ מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ נָ֔א וּבָשֵׁ֥ל מְבֻשָּׁ֖ל בַּמָּ֑יִם כִּ֣י אִם־צְלִי־אֵ֔שׁ רֹאשׁ֥וֹ עַל־כְּרָעָ֖יו וְעַל־קִרְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Do not eat from it raw or boiled, boiled in water, but rather roasted [with] fire, its head with its legs and with its inner parts.
pieces: None of it is to be eaten raw or stewed in water. It must be roasted in the fire whole, with its head, its legs, and its inner organs.

L.9: Do not eat any of it raw, or boiled, boiled in water, but roasted with fire, its head with its legs and with its inner parts.

R.9: Do not eat it raw, and do not boil it in water. Roast the whole animal over a fire, including its head, legs, and insides.

decisions.choice: boiled, boiled in water: in no way cooked in water
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated for emphasis: the meat must not be cooked in water at all, only roasted.

decisions.choice: its head with its legs and its inner parts: the animal roasted whole
decisions.reason: The animal is cooked in one piece, not cut up into portions. Verse 46 adds that none of its bones may be broken.

decisions.choice: whole
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "whole", which the list of head, legs and inner parts implies.

records.source: וְלֹא־תוֹתִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־בֹּ֑קֶר וְהַנֹּתָ֥ר מִמֶּ֛נּוּ עַד־בֹּ֖קֶר בָּאֵ֥שׁ תִּשְׂרֹֽפוּ׃
records.gloss: And not you will leave from it until morning; and the [part] remaining from it until morning in the fire you will burn.
pieces: None of it may be kept until morning; whatever is still uneaten at daybreak must be burned in the fire.

L.10: And you shall not leave any of it until morning; and what remains of it until morning you shall burn with fire.

R.10: Eat all of it that night. If any is left the next morning, you must burn it.

decisions.choice: burn what remains: the meal is not kept for ordinary use
decisions.reason: Leftovers of some holy meals had to be burned, not saved and eaten later (29:34; Leviticus 7:15). The Passover is eaten in one night and finished.

decisions.choice: Eat all of it that night
decisions.reason: Readable states the command positively: leaving nothing until morning means eating it all that night.

records.source: וְכָכָה֮ תֹּאכְל֣וּ אֹתוֹ֒ מָתְנֵיכֶ֣ם חֲגֻרִ֔ים נַֽעֲלֵיכֶם֙ בְּרַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם וּמַקֶּלְכֶ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ בְּחִפָּז֔וֹן פֶּ֥סַח ה֖וּא לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And thus you will eat it: your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you will eat it in haste. A passover it [is] to Yahweh.
pieces: When you eat it, be ready to set out: robes tucked into your belts, sandals on, staffs in hand. Eat it quickly. It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s Passover.

L.11: And thus you shall eat it: your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste. It [is] a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: Eat the meal dressed and ready to leave. Tie up your robes, put on your sandals, and hold your staff. Eat fast. This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s Passover.

decisions.choice: your loins girded: robe tied up at the waist, ready to travel
decisions.reason: A long robe was gathered up and tucked into a belt so that a person could walk, run or work freely (1 Kings 18:46; 2 Kings 4:29). With sandals on and staff in hand, they are to eat as people about to leave.

decisions.choice: in haste: in a hurry, with urgency
decisions.reason: The word means hurried flight and can carry a sense of alarm. Deuteronomy 16:3 uses it of the departure: "you came out of the land of Egypt in haste".

decisions.choice: Passover: named for Yahweh passing over the houses of Israel
decisions.reason: This is the first use of the noun. It comes from the verb used in verses 13, 23 and 27 for what Yahweh does at the houses marked with blood. The noun names the feast, the animal that is slaughtered (verse 21) and the sacrifice (verse 27). On the sense of the verb, "pass over" or "protect", see verse 13.

decisions.choice: robes tucked into your belts / Tie up your robes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain "loins girded" (m1). Literal keeps the idiom.

records.source: וְעָבַרְתִּ֣י בְאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַיִם֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַזֶּה֒ וְהִכֵּיתִ֤י כָל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מֵאָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֑ה וּבְכָל־אֱלֹהֵ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה שְׁפָטִ֖ים אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will pass through in [the] land of Egypt in this night, and I will strike every firstborn in [the] land of Egypt, from man and to beast; and on all [the] gods of Egypt I will do judgments. I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: This very night I will go through the land of Egypt and strike down every firstborn in it, human and animal alike. Against all the gods of Egypt I will carry out judgments. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: And I will pass through the land of Egypt in this night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments. I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: That night I will go through Egypt. I will kill the oldest son in every family and every firstborn male animal. I will judge all the gods of Egypt. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: pass through: go across the land
decisions.reason: This is the ordinary verb for crossing or going through a place. It is a different word from the one in verse 13, "pass over", which gives the Passover its name.

decisions.choice: against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments
decisions.reason: The last plague is a judgment on the gods Egypt trusted, which cannot protect even Pharaoh's son. Numbers 33:4 looks back on it: "on their gods also Yahweh executed judgments".

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh: God's name sets his seal on the word
decisions.reason: The same short declaration closes many of God's words to Moses (6:2, 6, 8, 29). The judgment will show who Yahweh is (7:5).

decisions.choice: the oldest son in every family and every firstborn male animal
decisions.reason: Readable says "oldest son" for people, as in 11:5, and spells out that the firstborn of animals are the males.

records.source: וְהָיָה֩ הַדָּ֨ם לָכֶ֜ם לְאֹ֗ת עַ֤ל הַבָּתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם שָׁ֔ם וְרָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וּפָסַחְתִּ֖י עֲלֵכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה בָכֶ֥ם נֶ֨גֶף֙ לְמַשְׁחִ֔ית בְּהַכֹּתִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And will be the blood for you for a sign on the houses where you [are] there; and I will see the blood and pass over you, and there will not be on you a plague for destruction when I strike in [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: The blood will mark the houses where you are staying; it will be a sign for you. I will see the blood and pass over you, and the plague that destroys will not fall on you when I strike the land of Egypt.

L.13: And the blood shall be for you a sign on the houses where you [are]; and I will see the blood and I will pass over you, and no plague shall be on you for destruction when I strike the land of Egypt.

R.13: The blood on your houses will be a sign for you. I will see the blood, and I will pass over you. The deadly plague will not touch you when I strike Egypt.

decisions.choice: pass over: go past and spare
decisions.reason: The verb is the root of "Passover" (verse 11). Here and in verses 23 and 27 it most likely means to pass by a house and spare it. It may instead mean to stand over a house to protect it: Isaiah 31:5 uses it of Yahweh guarding Jerusalem like birds hovering over their young. Verse 23, where Yahweh passes over the door and keeps the destroyer out, fits either sense.

decisions.choice: a sign for you: a mark that assures Israel
decisions.reason: The blood is a sign "for you". God sees it, but it is given for Israel's sake, as a pledge that they will be spared.

decisions.choice: a plague for destruction: a deadly blow
decisions.reason: "Destruction" is the same word that names "the destroyer" in verse 23.

decisions.choice: deadly
decisions.reason: Readable says "deadly" for "for destruction": the plague is the death of the firstborn.

records.source: וְהָיָה֩ הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ לְזִכָּר֔וֹן וְחַגֹּתֶ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ חַ֣ג לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם תְּחָגֻּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And will be this day for you a memorial, and you will celebrate it [as] a feast to Yahweh; throughout your generations, [as] a statute forever, you will celebrate it.
pieces: This day is to be one you remember. Hold a feast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on it, generation after generation, as a statute for all time.

L.14: And this day shall be for you a memorial, and you shall celebrate it [as] a feast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; throughout your generations, [as] a statute forever, you shall celebrate it.

R.14: You must always remember this day. Every year, celebrate it as a festival for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Your children and their children must keep this law forever.

decisions.choice: memorial: something that makes people remember
decisions.reason: The day is to be a reminder kept each year, so that every generation remembers what Yahweh did (13:9).

decisions.choice: a feast ... a statute forever: a festival fixed by law for all time
decisions.reason: The "feast" is a festival of celebration in honor of God. "Statute" is a fixed rule, and "forever" means for all time to come, for as long as the generations of Israel continue.

decisions.choice: Every year
decisions.reason: The feast is kept once a year (13:10), so Readable says so.

records.source: שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ מַצּ֣וֹת תֹּאכֵ֔לוּ אַ֚ךְ בַּיּ֣וֹם הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן תַּשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ שְּׂאֹ֖ר מִבָּתֵּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י׀כָּל־אֹכֵ֣ל חָמֵ֗ץ וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִיּ֥וֹם הָרִאשֹׁ֖ן עַד־י֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִעִֽי׃
records.gloss: Seven days unleavened bread you will eat; surely on the first day you will remove leaven from your houses, for anyone eating leavened [bread], that person will be cut off from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
pieces: Unleavened bread is to be your food for seven days. On the first day, without fail, rid your houses of leaven. Anyone who eats leavened bread at any time from the first day to the seventh will be cut off from Israel.

L.15: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; indeed, on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses, for anyone who eats what is leavened, that person shall be cut off from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.

R.15: For seven days, you must eat bread made without yeast. On the first day, get all the yeast out of your homes. Anyone who eats bread made with yeast during those seven days will be cut off from Israel.

decisions.choice: that person shall be cut off from Israel
alternatives: shall be excluded from the community
decisions.reason: The phrase is used often in the Law for grave offences. Its exact meaning is uncertain. It may mean that God himself will end the person's life or line, or that the person is to be excluded from the people of Israel. The text does not say that the community carries it out.

decisions.choice: leaven ... leavened: fermented dough, and bread raised with it
decisions.reason: Leaven was a piece of old, fermented dough kept back to make new dough rise. For the seven days, both the leaven itself and anything made with it are forbidden.

decisions.choice: yeast
decisions.reason: Readable says "yeast" for leaven, as in verse 8.

records.source: וּבַיּ֤וֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ מִקְרָא־קֹ֔דֶשׁ וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י מִקְרָא־קֹ֖דֶשׁ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם כָּל־מְלָאכָה֙ לֹא־יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה בָהֶ֔ם אַ֚ךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵאָכֵ֣ל לְכָל־נֶ֔פֶשׁ ה֥וּא לְבַדּ֖וֹ יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And on the first day a holy convocation, and on the seventh day a holy convocation will be for you; any work will not be done on them; only what will be eaten by every person, that alone may be done by you.
pieces: The first day and the seventh day are each to be a holy convocation for you, days when no work is done. The only work allowed is getting food ready, so that everyone can eat.

L.16: And on the first day [there shall be] a holy convocation, and on the seventh day a holy convocation shall be for you; no work shall be done on them; only what every person eats, that alone may be done by you.

R.16: On the first day and on the seventh day, the people must come together for a holy gathering. Do not do any work on those days. You may only cook food for people to eat.

decisions.choice: holy convocation: a sacred assembly called together
decisions.reason: A "convocation" is a calling together. On these days the people are summoned to gather for worship, and the day is set apart for God (Leviticus 23:2-8).

decisions.choice: only what every person eats: preparing food is allowed
decisions.reason: Unlike the Sabbath, when food was to be baked and cooked the day before (16:23), these feast days allow the work needed to prepare meals.

decisions.choice: come together for a holy gathering
decisions.reason: Readable explains "convocation" as a gathering the people come to.

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֮ אֶת־הַמַּצּוֹת֒ כִּ֗י בְּעֶ֨צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶת־צִבְאוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֖ם חֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will keep the unleavened bread, for on this very day I brought out your hosts from [the] land of Egypt; and you will keep this day throughout your generations [as] a statute forever.
pieces: Observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread, since this is the very day I led your ranks out of the land of Egypt. Keep this day in every generation as a statute for all time.

L.17: And you shall keep the unleavened bread, for on this very day I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt; and you shall keep this day throughout your generations [as] a statute forever.

R.17: Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. On this day I led your people out of Egypt like an army marching in groups. So celebrate this day every year as a law that lasts forever.

decisions.choice: keep the unleavened bread: observe the feast of unleavened bread
decisions.reason: "The unleavened bread" stands for the seven-day feast named for it (23:15). The verb "keep" can also mean "guard", and some have read it as guarding the dough from leaven, but the parallel "keep this day" later in the verse points to keeping the feast.

decisions.choice: I brought out: spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The exodus has not yet happened when these words are given. The verb speaks of it as complete, from the view of the later feasts that will remember it, or as certain to come.

decisions.choice: your hosts: Israel in its divisions, like an army
decisions.reason: The word means armies or companies. Israel leaves Egypt in ordered ranks, tribe by tribe (6:26; 7:4; 12:41, 51).

decisions.choice: the Feast of Unleavened Bread / Festival
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the feast (m1). Literal keeps "the unleavened bread".

records.source: בָּרִאשֹׁ֡ן בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֤וֹם לַחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב תֹּאכְל֖וּ מַצֹּ֑ת עַ֠ד י֣וֹם הָאֶחָ֧ד וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ בָּעָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: In the first [month], on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, you will eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.
pieces: From the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month to the evening of the twenty-first, you are to eat unleavened bread.

L.18: In the first [month], on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month, in the evening.

R.18: Eat bread made without yeast from the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month until the evening of the twenty-first day.

decisions.choice: from evening to evening: seven full days
decisions.reason: A day was counted from one evening to the next, so the evening of the fourteenth to the evening of the twenty-first makes the seven days of verse 15.

decisions.choice: in the first: the first month
decisions.reason: The word "month" is understood from the rest of the verse. It is the month of verse 2.

records.source: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים שְׂאֹ֕ר לֹ֥א יִמָּצֵ֖א בְּבָתֵּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י׀כָּל־אֹכֵ֣ל מַחְמֶ֗צֶת וְנִכְרְתָ֞ה הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַהִוא֙ מֵעֲדַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגֵּ֖ר וּבְאֶזְרַ֥ח הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Seven days leaven not will be found in your houses; for anyone eating leavened [food], that person will be cut off from [the] congregation of Israel, whether a sojourner or a native of the land.
pieces: For seven days there must be no leaven anywhere in your houses. Anyone who eats food made with leaven will be cut off from the community of Israel, whether a foreigner living among you or one born in the land.

L.19: Seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses; for anyone who eats what is leavened, that person shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether sojourner or native of the land.

R.19: For seven days, there must be no yeast in your homes. Anyone who eats food made with yeast will be cut off from the community of Israel. This is true for foreigners who live among you and for people born Israelites.

decisions.choice: sojourner: a foreigner living among Israel
decisions.reason: A sojourner is someone who has settled among a people not his own, without the rights of a native. The same law binds sojourner and native alike (verses 48-49). On "cut off", see verse 15.

decisions.choice: native of the land: one born in Israel
decisions.reason: "The land" looks ahead to the land Yahweh will give (verse 25). The rule is written for the time when Israel lives there with foreigners among them.

decisions.choice: foreigners who live among you ... people born Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable explains "sojourner" and "native of the land".

records.source: כָּל־מַחְמֶ֖צֶת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ בְּכֹל֙ מוֹשְׁבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם תֹּאכְל֖וּ מַצּֽוֹת׃פ
records.gloss: Anything leavened you will not eat; in all your dwellings you will eat unleavened bread.
pieces: Nothing leavened is to be eaten; in every place where you live, your bread is to be unleavened.'"

L.20: Any leavened thing you shall not eat; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.'"

R.20: Do not eat anything made with yeast. No matter where you live, you must eat bread without yeast.'"

decisions.choice: your dwellings: wherever you live
decisions.reason: The law applies in every home and settlement of Israel, not only at one holy place.

decisions.choice: the words of Yahweh end here
decisions.reason: Yahweh's words that began in verse 2, and the words Moses and Aaron are to pass on that began in verse 3, end with this verse. In verse 21 Moses speaks to the elders.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה לְכָל־זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֑ם מִֽשְׁכ֗וּ וּקְח֨וּ לָכֶ֥ם צֹ֛אן לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתֵיכֶ֖ם וְשַׁחֲט֥וּ הַפָּֽסַח׃
records.gloss: And summoned Moses all [the] elders of Israel and said to them, draw out and take for yourselves a flock animal for your clans, and slaughter the passover.
pieces: So Moses summoned all the elders of Israel. "Go and choose lambs from the flock, one for each of your clans," he told them, "and slaughter the Passover lamb.

L.21: And Moses called all the elders of Israel and said to them, "Draw out and take for yourselves [animals of the] flock for your clans, and slaughter the Passover.

R.21: Then Moses called together all the leaders of Israel. He told them, "Go and pick out a lamb or a young goat for each of your families. Kill it as the Passover lamb.

decisions.choice: draw out and take: go and pick out
decisions.reason: "Draw out" may mean to lead an animal out of the flock, or simply to go and act at once (compare Judges 4:6). Either way the elders are told to choose the animals.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the Passover animal
decisions.reason: Here the noun names the animal killed for the feast (2 Chronicles 30:15; 35:1).

decisions.choice: elders: the heads of Israel's families and clans
decisions.reason: The elders lead the people (3:16; 4:29). Moses gives them God's word to pass on to every household.

decisions.choice: the Passover lamb
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "lamb", since the noun here means the animal (m2). Literal keeps "the Passover".

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", which is what they were.

records.heading: Moses instructs the elders

records.source: וּלְקַחְתֶּ֞ם אֲגֻדַּ֣ת אֵז֗וֹב וּטְבַלְתֶּם֮ בַּדָּ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־בַּסַּף֒ וְהִגַּעְתֶּ֤ם אֶל־הַמַּשְׁקוֹף֙ וְאֶל־שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּזֹ֔ת מִן־הַדָּ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּסָּ֑ף וְאַתֶּ֗ם לֹ֥א תֵצְא֛וּ אִ֥ישׁ מִפֶּֽתַח־בֵּית֖וֹ עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: And you will take a bunch of hyssop and dip [it] in the blood that [is] in the basin, and touch to the lintel and to the two doorposts from the blood that [is] in the basin; and you, not will go out anyone from [the] door of his house until morning.
pieces: Dip a bundle of hyssop into the blood in the basin, and with it brush the blood onto the lintel and the two doorposts. Then no one is to step outside the house until morning.

L.22: And you shall take a bunch of hyssop and dip [it] in the blood that [is] in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with some of the blood that [is] in the basin; and as for you, none shall go out of the door of his house until morning.

R.22: Take a small bundle of hyssop plants, dip it into the blood in the bowl, and brush the blood on the top and both sides of the door frame. Nobody may leave the house until morning.

decisions.choice: hyssop: a small bushy plant
decisions.reason: Its exact kind is uncertain; it may be a plant of the marjoram family. Bunches of it were later used for sprinkling blood and water in cleansing (Leviticus 14:4; Numbers 19:18).

decisions.choice: basin: a bowl, or perhaps the threshold
decisions.reason: The word can mean a basin or bowl (2 Samuel 17:28; 1 Kings 7:50) or the threshold of a door (Judges 19:27). If "threshold" is meant, the lamb was killed at the doorway and its blood lay at the door.

decisions.choice: none shall go out: all stay inside until morning
decisions.reason: "You" is stressed. Safety is inside the house marked with blood; no one is to leave until the night is over.

records.source: וְעָבַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לִנְגֹּ֣ף אֶת־מִצְרַיִם֒ וְרָאָ֤ה אֶת־הַדָּם֙ עַל־הַמַּשְׁק֔וֹף וְעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֣י הַמְּזוּזֹ֑ת וּפָסַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ עַל־הַפֶּ֔תַח וְלֹ֤א יִתֵּן֙ הַמַּשְׁחִ֔ית לָבֹ֥א אֶל־בָּתֵּיכֶ֖ם לִנְגֹּֽף׃
records.gloss: And will pass through Yahweh to strike Egypt, and he will see the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, and will pass over Yahweh over the door, and not will allow the destroyer to come into your houses to strike.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will pass through to strike Egypt, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees the blood on the lintel and on both doorposts, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pass over that doorway and not allow the destroyer into your houses to strike you.

L.23: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will pass through to strike Egypt, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will see the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will pass over the door and will not allow the destroyer to come into your houses to strike [you].

R.23: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will go through Egypt to kill the Egyptians' firstborn. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will see the blood on the top and sides of your door frames, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pass over your door. He will not let the destroyer come into your houses to kill you.

decisions.choice: the destroyer: the one who brings death, under Yahweh's control
decisions.reason: In verse 12 and 12:29 Yahweh himself strikes the firstborn; here "the destroyer" strikes, but only where Yahweh allows. Elsewhere a destroying angel is sent by Yahweh (2 Samuel 24:16). The text does not say whether the destroyer is a separate being or another way of speaking of Yahweh's own act.

decisions.choice: pass over the door: spare, and guard, the house
decisions.reason: Yahweh passes over the doorway and keeps the destroyer from entering. See verse 13 on the sense of the verb.

decisions.choice: to kill the Egyptians' firstborn
decisions.reason: Readable names what the striking is, from verse 12.

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה לְחָק־לְךָ֥ וּלְבָנֶ֖יךָ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will keep this word as a statute for you and for your sons until forever.
pieces: You and your descendants are to keep this command as a statute for all time.

L.24: And you shall keep this word as a statute for you and for your {{gender:children|sons}} forever.

R.24: You and your children after you must obey these rules forever.

decisions.choice: this word: this command, the Passover rite
decisions.reason: "Word" here means the instruction just given: the lamb, the blood and staying indoors.

decisions.choice: your sons: your children and descendants
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means the generations to come, daughters as well as sons.

records.source: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־תָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And it will be when you come into the land that Yahweh will give to you, as he said, and you will keep this service.
pieces: And once you have come into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give you, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said, you are to go on keeping this service.

L.25: And it shall be, when you come into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give you, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken, that you shall keep this service.

R.25: When you come into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is giving you, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised, you must keep doing this act of worship.

decisions.choice: this service: this act of worship
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "serve". Israel's "service" in Egypt was forced labor (1:14; 2:23); now the word is used of their service to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: as he has spoken: the promise of the land
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised the land to the patriarchs and to Israel (3:8, 17; 6:8).

decisions.choice: act of worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for "service", as it does for serving God elsewhere in Exodus.

records.source: וְהָיָ֕ה כִּֽי־יֹאמְר֥וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּנֵיכֶ֑ם מָ֛ה הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it will be when say to you your sons, what [is] this service to you?
pieces: In time your children will say to you, 'What is this service of yours about?'

L.26: And it shall be, when your {{gender:children|sons}} say to you, 'What [is] this service to you?'

R.26: Someday your children will ask you, 'Why do you do this act of worship?'

decisions.choice: what is this service to you: what does it mean, why do you keep it
decisions.reason: The children ask the meaning of the rite. The same pattern of a child's question and a parent's answer is found in 13:14 and Deuteronomy 6:20.

decisions.choice: your sons: your children
decisions.reason: Daughters as well as sons are meant.

records.source: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֡ם זֶֽבַח־פֶּ֨סַח ה֜וּא לַֽיהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּ֠סַח עַל־בָּתֵּ֤י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם בְּנָגְפּ֥וֹ אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְאֶת־בָּתֵּ֣ינוּ הִצִּ֑יל וַיִּקֹּ֥ד הָעָ֖ם וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And you will say, [the] sacrifice of [the] passover it [is] to Yahweh, who passed over [the] houses of [the] sons of Israel in Egypt when he struck Egypt, and our houses he delivered. And bowed the people and worshiped.
pieces: Then you are to tell them, 'This is the sacrifice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s Passover. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck Egypt, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} passed over the houses of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} there and rescued our homes.'" At this the people bowed low and worshiped.

L.27: then you shall say, 'It [is] the sacrifice of the Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who passed over the houses of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel in Egypt when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck Egypt, and our houses {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delivered.'" And the people bowed low and worshiped.

R.27: Tell them, 'It is the Passover sacrifice for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck Egypt, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} passed over the houses of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. He saved our families.'" Then the people bowed down and worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice of the Passover: an offering slaughtered and eaten
decisions.reason: The word means an animal slaughtered as an offering, whose meat the worshipers eat (10:25; 18:12). The answer names the rite and tells the event behind it.

decisions.choice: our houses he delivered: he rescued our households
decisions.reason: The verb means to snatch away or rescue (3:8; 6:6). Later generations say "our houses", counting themselves among those who were spared. "Houses" means the households as well as the buildings.

decisions.choice: bowed low and worshiped: knelt and bowed to the ground
decisions.reason: Two verbs of bowing are joined, as in 4:31: bending the head low and bowing down to the ground in worship.

decisions.choice: worshiped the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the one they worshiped, as in 4:31.

records.source: וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And went and did [the] sons of Israel; just as commanded Yahweh Moses and Aaron, so they did.
pieces: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} went and did it. They did exactly as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses and Aaron.

L.28: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went and did [it]; just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

R.28: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} went and did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses and Aaron.

decisions.choice: just as ... so they did: complete obedience
decisions.reason: The pattern marks exact obedience to Yahweh's command (7:6, 10, 20; 39:32; 40:16).

decisions.choice: went and did: they set about doing it
decisions.reason: The verse sums up Israel's obedience to the instructions, which were carried out over the days from the tenth to the fourteenth of the month (verses 3-6).

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֗יְלָה וַֽיהוָה֮ הִכָּ֣ה כָל־בְּכוֹר֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ מִבְּכֹ֤ר פַּרְעֹה֙ הַיֹּשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְא֔וֹ עַ֚ד בְּכ֣וֹר הַשְּׁבִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית הַבּ֑וֹר וְכֹ֖ל בְּכ֥וֹר בְּהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] middle of the night, and Yahweh struck down every firstborn in [the] land of Egypt, from [the] firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to [the] firstborn of the captive who [was] in [the] house of the pit, and every firstborn of livestock.
pieces: In the middle of the night {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, the king on his throne, down to the firstborn of the captive locked in the dungeon, along with every firstborn among the animals.

L.29: And it was at the middle of the night, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who [was] in the house of the pit, and every firstborn of [the] livestock.

R.29: At midnight {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck down every oldest son in Egypt. Pharaoh, who ruled from his throne, lost his oldest son. So did the prisoner shut away in a dungeon. The firstborn males of the animals died as well.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the night Yahweh struck: the warning of 11:4-6 is carried out
decisions.reason: Moses had told Pharaoh that about midnight God would go out through Egypt and every firstborn would die (11:4-5). Now it happens, at the hour named, and the narrator says plainly that Yahweh struck them down (12:12, 23).

decisions.choice: the captive in the house of the pit: a prisoner in a dungeon, the lowest in the land
decisions.reason: "The house of the pit" is a prison, perhaps a cistern used as a cell (Genesis 40:15; 41:14; Jeremiah 37:16). In 11:5 the lowest person named was the slave woman at the millstones; here it is a captive. Either way the sense is the same: from the highest to the lowest, no household was spared.

decisions.choice: who sat on his throne: Pharaoh, the one reigning
alternatives: the firstborn who was to sit on his throne
decisions.reason: As in 11:5, the phrase most naturally describes Pharaoh himself, the king on his throne. It could also describe the firstborn as the heir who would sit on the throne; either way the royal house is struck.

decisions.choice: the king on his throne / locked in the dungeon; oldest son
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "dungeon" for "the house of the pit". Readable says "oldest son" for people, as in 4:23 and 11:5, and "firstborn males" for animals. Balanced says "the king" to show who sat on the throne.

records.heading: Every firstborn is struck down

records.source: וַיָּ֨קָם פַּרְעֹ֜ה לַ֗יְלָה ה֤וּא וְכָל־עֲבָדָיו֙ וְכָל־מִצְרַ֔יִם וַתְּהִ֛י צְעָקָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־אֵ֣ין בַּ֔יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵֽין־שָׁ֖ם מֵֽת׃
records.gloss: And rose Pharaoh [by] night, he and all his servants and all Egypt, and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there [was] not a house where there [was] not there a dead [one].
pieces: Pharaoh got up in the night, and so did all his officials and every Egyptian. A great cry of grief went up across Egypt, because no house was without its dead.

L.30: And Pharaoh rose up by night, he and all his servants and all Egypt; and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

R.30: That night Pharaoh woke up, and so did all his officials and all the Egyptians. Loud crying filled Egypt, because someone had died in every single home.

decisions.choice: a great cry: the cry foretold in 11:6
decisions.reason: Moses had said there would be "a great cry" in Egypt such as had never been (11:6). The word is the one used of Israel's cry under their slave drivers (3:7, 9); now the cry is Egypt's.

decisions.choice: not a house where there was not one dead: every household had a death
decisions.reason: The double negative is emphatic: every Egyptian household lost someone. Since only firstborn died (verse 29), it means every household had a firstborn among its members, or that the death reached every home.

decisions.choice: officials; cry of grief / loud crying
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are his officials (11:3, 8). The cry is mourning for the dead, as in 11:6; Literal keeps "cry".

records.source: וַיִּקְרָא֩ לְמֹשֶׁ֨ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֜ן לַ֗יְלָה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ ק֤וּמוּ צְּאוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ עַמִּ֔י גַּם־אַתֶּ֖ם גַּם־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּלְכ֛וּ עִבְד֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה כְּדַבֶּרְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And he summoned Moses and Aaron [by] night and said, rise, go out from among my people, both you and [the] sons of Israel, and go, serve Yahweh as you said.
pieces: While it was still night, Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said, "Up! Get out from among my people, you and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} with you! Go and serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as you have been saying.

L.31: And he called for Moses and Aaron by night and said, "Rise up, go out from among my people, both you and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; and go, serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as you have spoken.

R.31: That same night Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron. He said, "Get up! Get away from my people, you and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}! Go and worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the way you asked.

decisions.choice: he summoned Moses and Aaron by night: Pharaoh gives way
decisions.reason: Pharaoh had told Moses never to see his face again (10:28). Now he sends for him in the night. Moses had said Pharaoh's officials would come and tell him to go (11:8); Pharaoh himself orders it.

decisions.choice: as you said: without the limits Pharaoh set before
decisions.reason: Pharaoh had tried to keep back the children (10:10-11) and then the livestock (10:24). Now he lets everyone go on Moses' terms, as Moses had asked from the start (5:1; 10:9).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he summoned"; Balanced and Readable name Pharaoh, who is the subject from verse 30.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for "serve" here, as in 10:24, because the service meant is worship. Literal and Balanced keep "serve".

records.source: גַּם־צֹאנְכֶ֨ם גַּם־בְּקַרְכֶ֥ם קְח֛וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּרְתֶּ֖ם וָלֵ֑כוּ וּבֵֽרַכְתֶּ֖ם גַּם־אֹתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Also your flocks, also your herds take, as you said, and go; and you will bless also me.
pieces: Take your flocks and your herds as well, as you demanded, and be gone. And ask a blessing for me too."

L.32: Also your flocks, also your herds take, as you have spoken, and go; and bless me also."

R.32: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle with you, just as you wanted, and leave. And pray that I will be blessed too."

decisions.choice: your flocks and your herds, as you said: the last condition is dropped
decisions.reason: In 10:24 Pharaoh would let the people go only if the livestock stayed behind, and Moses refused (10:25-26). Now Pharaoh gives in on that too.

decisions.choice: bless me also: ask God's blessing on me
decisions.reason: To bless someone is to call down good on them, here by asking Yahweh. The king who had asked Moses to entreat Yahweh to remove the plagues (8:4, 24; 9:28; 10:17) now asks to be blessed as Israel goes. Whether he means it as a plea or a parting word is not said.

decisions.choice: pray that I will be blessed
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that the blessing is asked of God. Balanced says "ask a blessing for me"; Literal keeps "bless me". Readable says "sheep, goats, and cattle" for flocks and herds, as in 10:24.

records.source: וַתֶּחֱזַ֤ק מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ עַל־הָעָ֔ם לְמַהֵ֖ר לְשַׁלְּחָ֣ם מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ כֻּלָּ֥נוּ מֵתִֽים׃
records.gloss: And urged Egypt on the people to hurry to send them away from the land, for they said, all of us [are] dead.
pieces: The Egyptians pressed the people to leave the land with all speed. "We are as good as dead, every one of us!" they said.

L.33: And Egypt pressed the people to send them out from the land in haste, for they said, "All of us [are] dead!"

R.33: The Egyptians begged the Israelites to hurry out of the country. They said, "If you stay, we will all die!"

decisions.choice: urged: pressed hard, insisted
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Pharaoh's heart being made "strong" (7:13; 10:20). Here the Egyptians are strong, or insistent, on the people to go. The force that held Israel back now drives them out (6:1; 11:1).

decisions.choice: we are all dead: we will all die if they stay
decisions.reason: The Egyptians speak of their death as already happening. They fear that if Israel stays longer, death will come for all of them, not only the firstborn.

decisions.choice: If you stay
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition the Egyptians imply: their fear is of what will happen if Israel does not leave.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א הָעָ֛ם אֶת־בְּצֵק֖וֹ טֶ֣רֶם יֶחְמָ֑ץ מִשְׁאֲרֹתָ֛ם צְרֻרֹ֥ת בְּשִׂמְלֹתָ֖ם עַל־שִׁכְמָֽם׃
records.gloss: And took up the people their dough before it was leavened, their kneading bowls bound up in their cloaks on their shoulder.
pieces: So the people picked up their dough before it had a chance to rise and carried it on their shoulders, the kneading bowls tied up in their cloaks.

L.34: And the people carried their dough before it was leavened, their kneading bowls bound in their cloaks upon their shoulder.

R.34: So the people grabbed their bread dough before it had time to rise. They wrapped the bowls of dough in their clothes and carried them on their shoulders.

decisions.choice: before it was leavened: they left in such haste that the bread had no time to rise
decisions.reason: Leaven is a piece of fermented dough worked into new dough to make it rise. There was no time for that. This is why Israel eats unleavened bread at the feast (12:15-20, 39; Deuteronomy 16:3).

decisions.choice: kneading bowls bound in their cloaks: the dough carried wrapped in their outer garments
decisions.reason: A kneading bowl was a shallow trough for mixing dough (8:3). The cloak was a large outer garment, used also as a wrap and a bed covering (22:25-26). Carrying the bowls wrapped up on their shoulders shows how quickly they set out.

decisions.choice: rise
decisions.reason: "Leavened" means made to rise with leaven. Balanced and Readable say "rise"; Literal keeps "leavened".

records.source: וּבְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עָשׂ֖וּ כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַֽיִּשְׁאֲלוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם כְּלֵי־כֶ֛סֶף וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב וּשְׂמָלֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Israel did according to [the] word of Moses, and they asked from Egypt articles of silver and articles of gold and clothes.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} acted on Moses' word: they asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold, and for clothing.

L.35: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did according to the word of Moses, and they asked from the Egyptians articles of silver and articles of gold, and clothing.

R.35: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what Moses had told them. They asked the Egyptians for things made of silver and gold, and for clothes.

decisions.choice: asked: requested, and received as a gift
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 3:22 and 11:2, where God told the people to ask. It is a request granted freely, not a loan to be paid back.

decisions.choice: did ... asked: what they did may have been done before the night of the departure
decisions.reason: The verbs simply continue the story. The asking may have taken place in the days before this night, once Moses passed on the command of 11:2; the narrator tells it here, where it explains what they took with them.

records.source: וַֽיהוָ֞ה נָתַ֨ן אֶת־חֵ֥ן הָעָ֛ם בְּעֵינֵ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם וַיַּשְׁאִל֑וּם וַֽיְנַצְּל֖וּ אֶת־מִצְרָֽיִם׃פ
records.gloss: And Yahweh gave the favor of the people in [the] eyes of Egypt, and they granted them [their request]; and they plundered Egypt.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had made the Egyptians look kindly on the people, and they granted what was asked. So Israel stripped Egypt of its wealth.

L.36: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, and they let them have [what they asked]; and they plundered Egypt.

R.36: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the Egyptians friendly toward the Israelites, so they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way the Israelites took away the riches of Egypt.

decisions.choice: Yahweh gave the people favor: the promise of 3:21 is kept
decisions.reason: God had said, "I will give this people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, and when you go, you will not go empty-handed" (3:21; compare 11:3). Israel had been made to work for nothing; now they leave with wages (Genesis 15:14).

decisions.choice: they let them have it: the Egyptians granted the request
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of "ask": to let someone ask and have what they ask for. The Egyptians gave freely what was asked of them.

decisions.choice: plundered Egypt: took its wealth as spoil
decisions.reason: The verb is used of stripping something away, as spoil is taken after a battle (3:22; 2 Chronicles 20:25). Israel did not fight, yet they leave like a victorious army carrying the spoil of the defeated, because God fought for them.

decisions.choice: stripped Egypt of its wealth / took away the riches of Egypt
decisions.reason: As in 3:22. Literal keeps "plundered". Balanced and Readable name Israel as the subject of "plundered".

records.source: וַיִּסְע֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵרַעְמְסֵ֖ס סֻכֹּ֑תָה כְּשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֧לֶף רַגְלִ֛י הַגְּבָרִ֖ים לְבַ֥ד מִטָּֽף׃
records.gloss: And set out [the] sons of Israel from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot, the men, apart from little ones.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} set out from Rameses for Succoth. There were about 600,000 men on foot, not counting the little ones.

L.37: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth, about 600,000 on foot, the men, besides little ones.

R.37: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} traveled from Rameses to Succoth. There were about 600,000 men walking, as well as the children and the others who depended on them.

decisions.choice: about six hundred thousand: a very large number of men
alternatives: about six hundred clans or military units
decisions.reason: The word for "thousand" is the ordinary word for the number, and the census lists in Numbers give totals in the same range (Numbers 1:46; 11:21). But the same word can also mean a clan or a company of men (Judges 6:15; 1 Samuel 10:19; Micah 5:1), and some read it that way here, which would give a much smaller number. The text does not settle how the figure was counted. What is clear is that Israel had become a great people, as God had promised (1:7; Genesis 46:3).

decisions.choice: on foot, the men: adult men who could march
decisions.reason: The word means men on foot, often foot soldiers. It counts the grown men, as a muster for war would (Numbers 1:3; 11:21).

decisions.choice: little ones: children and others dependent on the men
decisions.reason: As in 10:10 and 10:24, the word covers the children and often the whole household who depended on the men, including the women.

decisions.choice: the children and the others who depended on them
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "little ones" covers. Literal and Balanced keep "little ones".

records.heading: Israel leaves Egypt

records.source: וְגַם־עֵ֥רֶב רַ֖ב עָלָ֣ה אִתָּ֑ם וְצֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר מִקְנֶ֖ה כָּבֵ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And also a mixed company numerous went up with them, and flock[s] and herd[s], livestock very heavy.
pieces: A large crowd of people of mixed descent went with them as well, and great numbers of animals, flocks and herds alike.

L.38: And also a great mixed multitude went up with them, and flocks and herds, very heavy livestock.

R.38: Many people who were not Israelites went with them too. They also took a huge number of sheep, goats, and cattle.

decisions.choice: a great mixed multitude: a large group of people who were not Israelites
decisions.reason: The word means a mixture. People of other origins left Egypt with Israel, perhaps Egyptians and other slaves who had seen what God had done (9:20). Numbers 11:4 speaks of them, and Leviticus 24:10 tells of a man with an Egyptian father. The rules in verses 43-49 show how such people could share in the Passover.

decisions.choice: very heavy livestock: a very great number of animals
decisions.reason: "Heavy" here means abundant, as of Abram's wealth (Genesis 13:2). Not a hoof was left behind (10:26).

decisions.choice: sheep, goats, and cattle
decisions.reason: Readable names the animals in flocks and herds, as in 10:9 and 10:24.

records.source: וַיֹּאפ֨וּ אֶת־הַבָּצֵ֜ק אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצִ֧יאוּ מִמִּצְרַ֛יִם עֻגֹ֥ת מַצּ֖וֹת כִּ֣י לֹ֣א חָמֵ֑ץ כִּֽי־גֹרְשׁ֣וּ מִמִּצְרַ֗יִם וְלֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ לְהִתְמַהְמֵ֔הַּ וְגַם־צֵדָ֖ה לֹא־עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they baked the dough which they had brought out from Egypt [into] cakes of unleavened bread, for not it was leavened, for they were driven out from Egypt and not they were able to delay, and also provisions not they had made for themselves.
pieces: From the dough they had carried out of Egypt they baked flat cakes of unleavened bread. It had not risen, since they had been driven out of Egypt with no chance to linger, and they had not got any food ready for the road.

L.39: And they baked the dough which they had brought out from Egypt [into] cakes of unleavened bread, for it was not leavened, because they had been driven out from Egypt and were not able to linger, and also they had not made provisions for themselves.

R.39: They used the dough they had brought from Egypt to bake flat loaves of unleavened bread, made without yeast. The dough had not risen, because the Egyptians had forced them to leave in a hurry. They could not wait, and they had not made any food for the trip.

decisions.choice: cakes of unleavened bread, because they were driven out: the first Feast of Unleavened Bread
decisions.reason: Israel ate unleavened bread on the way out because there was no time for the dough to rise. God had already commanded it for the Passover meal and the seven-day feast (12:8, 15-20), and Deuteronomy 16:3 calls it "the bread of affliction", eaten because they left Egypt in haste.

decisions.choice: driven out: as God had said
decisions.reason: God told Moses that Pharaoh would drive them out (6:1; 11:1). The word is the same.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians had forced them; made without yeast
decisions.reason: Readable names the Egyptians, who drove Israel out (verse 33), and explains "unleavened".

records.source: וּמוֹשַׁב֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And the dwelling of [the] sons of Israel which they dwelt in Egypt [was] thirty years and four hundred years.
pieces: The time the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} spent living in Egypt came to 430 years.

L.40: And the dwelling of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, which they dwelt in Egypt, [was] 430 years.

R.40: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had lived in Egypt for 430 years.

decisions.choice: which they dwelt in Egypt: the Hebrew text, which counts the 430 years in Egypt
alternatives: in Egypt and in the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Greek Septuagint add "and in the land of Canaan" (their wording and order differ slightly), so that the 430 years cover the time of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in Canaan as well as Israel's time in Egypt. Galatians 3:17 counts 430 years from the promise to Abraham to the giving of the law, which fits the longer reading. Genesis 15:13 gives a round 400 years of affliction in a foreign land. We follow the Hebrew text here.

decisions.choice: 430 years: God's word to Abraham comes true
decisions.reason: God told Abram that his descendants would be strangers in a land not their own and afflicted for 400 years, and then come out with great possessions (Genesis 15:13-14). The exact count here shows that the time God set has run its full course (verse 41).
The Hebrew says "thirty years and four hundred years". Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֶ֨צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה יָֽצְא֛וּ כָּל־צִבְא֥וֹת יְהוָ֖ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] end of thirty years and four hundred years, and it was on the bone of the day the this, went out all [the] hosts of Yahweh from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: When the 430 years were over, on that very same day, all the ranks of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} marched out of the land of Egypt.

L.41: And it was at the end of 430 years, and it was on this very day, [that] all the hosts of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} went out from the land of Egypt.

R.41: On the last day of those 430 years, all of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people left Egypt, marching out like an army.

decisions.choice: on the bone of this day: on this very day, to the day
decisions.reason: "The bone of the day" means the day itself, the exact day (Genesis 7:13; 17:23). The departure came at the very end of the period God had set, not a day late.

decisions.choice: the hosts of Yahweh: Israel as God's own ordered companies
decisions.reason: The word is used of armies. God called Israel "my hosts" in 7:4, and they go out "by their hosts" (6:26; 12:51). They leave Egypt as an organized people under God's command, not as a crowd of runaway slaves.

decisions.choice: ranks / like an army
decisions.reason: As in 6:26 and 7:4. Literal keeps "hosts"; Balanced says "ranks"; Readable says "people" and adds "like an army".

records.source: לֵ֣יל שִׁמֻּרִ֥ים הוּא֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לְהוֹצִיאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הֽוּא־הַלַּ֤יְלָה הַזֶּה֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה שִׁמֻּרִ֛ים לְכָל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: [A] night of vigils it [was] for Yahweh, to bring them out from [the] land of Egypt; it [is] the night the this for Yahweh, vigils for all [the] sons of Israel throughout their generations.
pieces: That was a night when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} kept watch, so as to bring them out of the land of Egypt. This same night belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are to keep watch on it, generation after generation.

L.42: A night of watching it [was] for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to bring them out from the land of Egypt; this [is] the night for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [a time of] watching for all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel throughout their generations.

R.42: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} stayed on watch all that night so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could lead them out of Egypt. So this night belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Every year on this night, all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must stay awake and remember. They must do this for all time to come.

decisions.choice: a night of watching for Yahweh: Yahweh kept watch that night, and Israel keeps it in turn
alternatives: a night to be observed for Yahweh
decisions.reason: The phrase "a night of watching for Yahweh" can mean a night when Yahweh kept watch over Israel to bring them out (compare Psalm 121:4), or a night to be watched, that is, observed, in his honor. The verse seems to use both: Yahweh watched that night, so Israel is to keep watch on this night for all generations.

decisions.choice: watching: keeping vigil, staying awake and alert
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "keep, watch" and occurs only in this verse. It is plural, which marks a full or solemn watch.

decisions.choice: throughout their generations: for all time to come
decisions.reason: The phrase means for every generation of Israel, as in 12:14 and 12:17.

decisions.choice: stay awake and remember; every year
decisions.reason: Readable explains what keeping watch means and that the night returns each year. This goes slightly beyond the Hebrew, which says only "watching".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן זֹ֖את חֻקַּ֣ת הַפָּ֑סַח כָּל־בֶּן־נֵכָ֖ר לֹא־יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses and Aaron, this [is the] statute of the Passover: any son of foreignness not will eat of it.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron, "This is the statute for the Passover. No foreigner is to eat of it.

L.43: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron, "This [is] the statute of the Passover: no son of a foreign land may eat of it.

R.43: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron, "Here are the rules for the Passover meal. No one from another nation may eat it.

decisions.choice: a son of foreignness: a foreigner who has not joined Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase means someone of foreign birth who remains an outsider to Israel and its covenant with God. Verse 48 shows that a foreigner who settles in Israel and is circumcised with his household may keep the Passover; what bars a person is not birth but being outside the covenant (Genesis 17:12-14).

decisions.choice: statute: a fixed rule
decisions.reason: The word means something decreed and set down, as in "a statute forever" (12:14, 17). Verses 43-49 add who may eat the Passover to the rules of verses 1-28; the mixed multitude of verse 38 makes the question a real one.

records.heading: Who may eat the Passover

records.source: וְכָל־עֶ֥בֶד אִ֖ישׁ מִקְנַת־כָּ֑סֶף וּמַלְתָּ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ אָ֖ז יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And every slave of [a] man, [the] purchase of silver, and you circumcise him, then he will eat of it.
pieces: A slave bought with money may share in it, but only after you have circumcised him.

L.44: But every man's slave, bought with silver, when you have circumcised him, then he may eat of it.

R.44: A slave someone has bought may eat the meal, but first he must be circumcised.

decisions.choice: a slave bought with silver, once circumcised, may eat: he belongs to the household
decisions.reason: A slave bought with money became part of the household, and God told Abraham that such slaves were to be circumcised with his family (Genesis 17:12-13). As a member of the household within the covenant, he shares in its Passover.

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Silver was the money of the time. Literal keeps "silver". Readable makes the sentence passive ("he must be circumcised") because the "you" is the household head.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: this slave was bought with money (m1).

records.source: תּוֹשָׁ֥ב וְשָׂכִ֖יר לֹא־יֹ֥אכַל־בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: A settler and a hired worker not will eat of it.
pieces: Neither a settler nor a hired laborer is to eat it.

L.45: A settler and a hired worker may not eat of it.

R.45: Someone who is only staying with you, or a worker you pay, must not eat it.

decisions.choice: settler: a foreign resident who lives among Israel without belonging to it
decisions.reason: The word means one who dwells or stays, a foreigner living in the land, often as a dependent (Leviticus 25:6, 35, 40). Unlike the bought slave, he is not part of an Israelite household, and unlike the sojourner of verse 48 he has not been circumcised to join the people.

decisions.choice: hired worker: a laborer paid by the day or the year
decisions.reason: A hired worker kept his own independence and household. Since he did not belong to the household he worked for, he did not share its Passover.

decisions.choice: someone who is only staying with you
decisions.reason: Readable explains "settler" by what makes him different: he lives with Israel but is not part of it.

records.source: בְּבַ֤יִת אֶחָד֙ יֵאָכֵ֔ל לֹא־תוֹצִ֧יא מִן־הַבַּ֛יִת מִן־הַבָּשָׂ֖ר ח֑וּצָה וְעֶ֖צֶם לֹ֥א תִשְׁבְּרוּ־בֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: In one house it will be eaten; not you will bring out from the house any of the meat outside, and a bone not you will break in it.
pieces: It is to be eaten within one house. No meat is to be carried outside the house, and you must not break a bone of it.

L.46: In one house it shall be eaten; you shall not bring out any of the meat from the house to the outside, and a bone you shall not break in it.

R.46: The whole meal must be eaten inside one house. No one may take any of the meat outside, and none of its bones may be broken.

decisions.choice: in one house: each lamb eaten whole by one household group
decisions.reason: Each lamb was shared by a household, or by small households joined together (12:3-4). It was all eaten in that one house, and nothing was carried away or left for later (12:10).

decisions.choice: a bone of it you shall not break: the lamb kept whole
decisions.reason: The rule is repeated in Numbers 9:12. Psalm 34:21 says God keeps all the bones of the righteous, not one broken. John 19:36 quotes these words of Jesus on the cross, whose legs were not broken.

decisions.choice: none of its bones may be broken
decisions.reason: Readable turns the commands into passive statements, since they apply to everyone at the meal.

records.source: כָּל־עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: All [the] congregation of Israel will do it.
pieces: The whole community of Israel is to keep it.

L.47: All the congregation of Israel shall do it.

R.47: Every Israelite must take part in the Passover.

decisions.choice: congregation: Israel gathered as one people
decisions.reason: The word means an assembly or community, the whole people as a body (12:3, 6). Keeping the Passover is not optional for any household in Israel (Numbers 9:13).

decisions.choice: do it: keep it, observe it
decisions.reason: To "do" a feast is to celebrate it, as in verse 48.

records.source: וְכִֽי־יָג֨וּר אִתְּךָ֜ גֵּ֗ר וְעָ֣שָׂה פֶסַח֮ לַיהוָה֒ הִמּ֧וֹל ל֣וֹ כָל־זָכָ֗ר וְאָז֙ יִקְרַ֣ב לַעֲשֹׂת֔וֹ וְהָיָ֖ה כְּאֶזְרַ֣ח הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכָל־עָרֵ֖ל לֹֽא־יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And when sojourns with you a sojourner and would do [a] Passover to Yahweh, let be circumcised to him every male, and then he may draw near to do it, and he will be like [the] native of the land; and any uncircumcised [man] not will eat of it.
pieces: Suppose a foreigner living among you wants to hold a Passover for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Every male in his household must first be circumcised. Then he may come near and keep it, and he will count as one born in the land. But anyone uncircumcised is not to eat of it.

L.48: And when a sojourner sojourns with you and would keep a Passover to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, let every male of his be circumcised, and then he may draw near to keep it, and he shall be like a native of the land; but no uncircumcised [man] may eat of it.

R.48: If a foreigner living among you wants to celebrate the Passover in honor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all the males in his family must first be circumcised. Then he may join in, as if he had been born an Israelite. But a man who is not circumcised must never eat this meal.

decisions.choice: a sojourner who sojourns with you: a foreigner who has settled among Israel
decisions.reason: A sojourner is someone living away from his own people, without the rights of the native-born, as Abraham was in Canaan (Genesis 23:4) and Israel was in Egypt (22:20; 23:9). Such a person could join fully in the Passover by being circumcised with his household.

decisions.choice: circumcised ... like a native of the land: joining the covenant people
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham (Genesis 17:10-14). A foreigner who receives it with his household stands like one born in Israel. What keeps someone from the Passover is being uncircumcised, not being foreign.

decisions.choice: foreigner living among you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "foreigner living among you" for "sojourner", a word few readers use; Literal keeps "sojourner".

decisions.choice: as if he had been born an Israelite
decisions.reason: "The native of the land" is an Israelite by birth. Readable says so.

records.source: תּוֹרָ֣ה אַחַ֔ת יִהְיֶ֖ה לָֽאֶזְרָ֑ח וְלַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: One law will be for the native and for the sojourner who sojourns among you.
pieces: One law is to govern both the native-born and the foreigner living among you."

L.49: One law shall be for the native and for the sojourner who sojourns among you."

R.49: The same rules apply to those born Israelites and to foreigners who live among you."

decisions.choice: law: instruction, a binding rule
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or instruction, and here a rule laid down by God. The same principle, one law for the native and the foreigner, is repeated in Leviticus 24:22 and Numbers 9:14 and 15:15-16.

decisions.choice: the native and the sojourner: one standing before God's law
decisions.reason: The circumcised foreigner keeps the Passover on the same terms as the Israelite by birth. Membership in God's people is open to those who join it, not limited by birth.

decisions.choice: the foreigner living among you
decisions.reason: As in verse 48; Literal keeps "the sojourner who sojourns".

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֖וּ כָּל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֖ן כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And did all [the] sons of Israel as commanded Yahweh Moses and Aaron; so they did.
pieces: All the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} carried out exactly what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses and Aaron.

L.50: And all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.

R.50: All the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} obeyed. They did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses and Aaron.

decisions.choice: they did ... so they did: full obedience
decisions.reason: Saying "they did" twice stresses that Israel obeyed completely, as 12:28 also says. It closes the Passover instructions before the story of the departure resumes.

decisions.choice: exactly / obeyed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the repeated "so they did" with one word of emphasis rather than repeating the verb; Literal keeps both.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י בְּעֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה הוֹצִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־צִבְאֹתָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And it was on the bone of the day the this, brought out Yahweh [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt by their hosts.
pieces: On that same day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} led the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of the land of Egypt, company by company.

L.51: And it was on this very day [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel out from the land of Egypt by their hosts.

R.51: On that very day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} led the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt in their groups, like an army.

decisions.choice: on this very day ... by their hosts: the departure told again
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 41, now with Yahweh as the one who brought them out. It fulfills God's command to bring Israel out "by their hosts" (6:26; 7:4) and leads into the rules about the firstborn in chapter 13.

decisions.choice: by their hosts: in organized companies, like an army
decisions.reason: As in 6:26, Israel leaves in ordered ranks, not as a fleeing crowd.

decisions.choice: company by company / in their groups, like an army
decisions.reason: As in 6:26. Literal keeps "by their hosts".
